subject: 83C2E82C31DB4115A3CDF5884D0CB19E
introduction: These hundred readings hold that God in His essence cannot be known, and that out of grace He makes Himself known through chosen human beings, the Manifestations, who stand between the Creator and creation as a mirror stands before the sun. Whoever knows them knows God; prayer is turned toward them; without such a mediator, the readings say, people worship an image made by their own minds. Many scriptures speak in the same way, of Moses standing between the Lord and the people, of one mediator, of a door and a way, of a God who speaks only from behind a veil or through a messenger. Other passages say that God is nearer than the jugular vein and hears whoever calls, and Paine, Emerson, Kabir, Seneca and the Buddha need no go-between. Both are set here beside the readings.
questions: The readings say the door to knowing God's essence is closed and that a mediator opens another. What do you find you can know of God, and how?
Job longed for someone who could lay a hand on both God and himself. What human need does a mediator answer?
The Qur’an says God is nearer than the jugular vein, and the psalm that He is near to all who call. How do the readings reconcile that nearness with the need for a Manifestation?
Paine and Emerson want an original relation with no one in between. What is strong in their position, and what do the readings say it risks?
The Buddha told his disciples to be lamps unto themselves. Is a mediator someone who does for you what you cannot do, or who shows you what you must do?
Several readings speak of turning toward the Manifestation in prayer. To whom do you address prayer, and what helps you focus?

outside.why: Jesus said: I am the door; by me if any man enter in, he shall be saved, and shall go in and out, and find pasture.
Zophar asks Job: canst thou by searching find out God? Canst thou find out the Almighty unto perfection?
The first letter to Timothy speaks of God dwelling in the light which no man can approach unto.
John's Gospel says: no man hath seen God at any time; the only begotten Son hath declared him.
Isaiah says: verily Thou art a God that hidest Thyself, O God of Israel, the Saviour.
Moses asked to see God's glory and was told: there shall no man see me, and live.
The Qur’an says that it is not given to any mortal that God should speak to him unless by revelation, or from behind a veil, or by sending a messenger.
Jesus said: neither knoweth any man the Father, save the Son, and he to whomsoever the Son will reveal him.
Job complains that God is not a man as he is, and that there is no daysman betwixt them who might lay his hand upon them both. What does Job's wish say about the human need these readings describe?
The Qur’an has God say of man: We are nearer to him than his jugular vein. If God is nearer than that, in what sense is the door of knowledge closed?
In John's Gospel Jesus says: this is life eternal, that they might know Thee, the only true God, and the one whom Thou hast sent.
Jesus said: I am the way, the truth, and the life; no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.
The Letter to the Hebrews calls the Son the brightness of God's glory and the express image of His person.
The Qur’an says in a single line that whoever obeys the messenger has obeyed God.
The Tao Te Ching begins: the Tao that can be trodden is not the enduring and unchanging Tao.
Plato compared the good to the sun, the author of visibility in all visible things, which is not itself what it makes visible.
In the Bhagavad Gita Arjuna is shown the divine form like the sunburst of a thousand suns, and is overwhelmed. What does a mirror give that the sun itself cannot?
The psalmist says that the heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament sheweth His handiwork.
Whitman found letters from God dropped in the street, every one signed by God's name. If all things tell of the light, why is one focal point needed?
The Letter to the Colossians calls Christ the image of the invisible God.
Jesus said to Philip: he that hath seen me hath seen the Father.
Jesus said: he that receiveth whomsoever I send receiveth me, and he that receiveth me receiveth Him that sent me.
Of Moses God says: with him will I speak mouth to mouth, and the similitude of the Lord shall he behold.
Isaiah asks: to whom then will ye liken God, or what likeness will ye compare unto Him?
Augustine asked the earth, the sea and the living creatures, and they answered: we are not your God; seek higher than we.
Exodus says that Moses put a vail on his face when he had done speaking with the people, and took it off when he went in before the Lord.
Paul speaks of the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.
The second commandment forbids any likeness of God. How is turning to a human being as the Veil above which nothing can be found kept from being what that commandment forbids?
In Isaiah God says: as the heavens are higher than the earth, so are my ways higher than your ways.
The psalmist says: such knowledge is too wonderful for me; it is high, I cannot attain unto it.
Jesus said: I and my Father are one, and pointed to the works he had shown from his Father.
John's Gospel begins: in the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God.
Paul says that the first man is of the earth, and that the natural comes first and afterward the spiritual.
The Letter to the Hebrews says that God spoke at sundry times and in divers manners in time past by the prophets.
The first letter to Timothy says that there is one God, and one mediator between God and men.
The Letter to the Hebrews calls Jesus the mediator of a better covenant, established upon better promises.
Malachi promises that the Sun of righteousness shall arise with healing in his wings.
John's Gospel says that the Word was made flesh and dwelt among us. How does a mediator who mirrors God differ from a God who becomes flesh?
The first letter of John says: we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous.
Paul says that God was in Christ, reconciling the world unto Himself.
Paul says that now we see through a glass, darkly, but then face to face.
The psalmist prays: O send out Thy light and Thy truth; let them lead me.
Xenophanes said that if oxen and horses had hands, horses would paint the gods like horses, and oxen like oxen.
In Isaiah God says: my glory will I not give to another, neither my praise to graven images.
Thomas Paine wrote: my own mind is my own church. What can be said to someone who is sure that they commune with God directly?

Emerson wrote that earlier generations beheld God and nature face to face, and we through their eyes, and asked why we should not also enjoy an original relation to the universe. What would be lost, and what gained, if each person looked only for themselves?

Jeremiah foresees a day when they shall teach no more every man his neighbour, saying, Know the Lord, for they shall all know me. Is the need for a mediator permanent, or does a mediator aim to make each person know for themselves?
The Qur’an has God say: when My servants question thee concerning Me, then surely I am nigh; I answer the prayer of the suppliant. Why is it not enough to turn to an omnipresent God directly?
Tennyson wrote: speak to Him thou for He hears; closer is He than breathing, and nearer than hands and feet. What does this confidence leave out, according to the readings?
The psalm says that the Lord is nigh unto all them that call upon Him in truth. How do nearness to all who call and knowledge through a Manifestation fit together?
Moses reminds Israel: I stood between the Lord and you at that time, to shew you the word of the Lord.
The Buddha told Ananda: be ye lamps unto yourselves; betake yourselves to no external refuge. Does every religion teach that a mediator is necessary?
At Sinai the people said to Moses: speak thou with us, and we will hear; but let not God speak with us, lest we die.
The Dhammapada says: by oneself the evil is done, by oneself one is purified; no one can purify another. What does a mediator do, if each must walk the path alone?
Moses foretold a prophet into whose mouth God would put His words.
The Qur’an says: for every nation there is a messenger, and it will be judged between them fairly.
Isaiah says that the people that walked in darkness have seen a great light.
John's Gospel speaks of the true Light, which lighteth every man that cometh into the world.
Jeremiah, who pleaded that he was a child, was told: whatsoever I command thee thou shalt speak.
Jesus said: my doctrine is not mine, but His that sent me.
Jesus said: the Son can do nothing of himself, but what he seeth the Father do.
Jesus said: I can of mine own self do nothing; I seek not mine own will, but the will of the Father.
Cyprian wrote that there are many rays of the sun, but one light, and the unity is preserved in the source.
The psalm calls the word of God a lamp unto the feet and a light unto the path.
Amos says that the Lord God will do nothing but He revealeth His secret unto His servants the prophets.
Jesus read in the synagogue: the Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach.
The people were astonished, for he taught them as one having authority, and not as the scribes.
The Qur’an describes its Prophet as a summoner unto God by His permission, and as a lamp that giveth light.
Jesus said of John the Baptist: he was a burning and a shining light.
John's Gospel says of the Baptist: he was not that Light, but was sent to bear witness of that Light. How does a lamp differ from the light, and why does the difference matter?
Paul says that we, beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image.
The Qur’an bids its Prophet say: I am only a mortal like you; it is inspired in me that your God is One.
Jesus asked: why callest thou me good? There is none good but one, that is, God.
The Qur’an tells the believers: turn thy face toward the Inviolable Place of Worship; wheresoever ye may be, turn your faces toward it.
Daniel kneeled three times a day at windows open toward Jerusalem, and prayed, and gave thanks.
The Letter to the Hebrews speaks of a new and living way opened through the veil.
Jesus said: whatsoever ye shall ask the Father in my name, He will give it you.
The Qur’an also says: unto God belong the East and the West, and whithersoever ye turn, there is God's countenance. Does prayer need a direction or an object to turn toward?
Jesus told a woman who asked where to worship that God is to be worshipped in spirit and in truth. What is the place of a focal point in prayer that is in spirit?
Jesus taught his disciples to enter into their closet and pray to their Father which is in secret. To whom is prayer addressed, and through whom?

The Letter to the Hebrews says that because we have a high priest who was tempted as we are, we may come boldly unto the throne of grace. Does a mediator stand between a person and God, or bring them closer?
The psalmist says to God: in Thy light shall we see light.
The Letter to the Hebrews pictures the living as compassed about with a great cloud of witnesses.
Peter said: God is no respecter of persons; in every nation he that feareth Him, and worketh righteousness, is accepted with Him. What of those who do right and have never turned to a Manifestation?
Jesus said: I am the vine, ye are the branches; without me ye can do nothing.
Through Isaiah God says: I will bring the blind by a way that they knew not.
At Lystra Paul and Barnabas rent their clothes when the crowd took them for gods, and said: we also are men of like passions with you.
When John fell at the angel's feet he was told: see thou do it not; I am thy fellowservant; worship God. How is high honour paid to a mediator kept distinct from worship?
Jacob dreamed of a ladder set up on the earth, whose top reached to heaven, and the angels of God ascending and descending on it.
Jesus said: strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life.
At Sinai Moses saw a bush that burned with fire and was not consumed, and was called by name out of it.
The prayer Jesus taught is addressed to the Father: Thy kingdom come, Thy will be done. How do you understand turning one's thoughts to a Manifestation while praying to God?
Kabir has God say: O servant, where dost thou seek Me? Lo, I am beside thee. What answer do the readings give to those who say they need no go-between?
The Qur’an has the believers say: we make no distinction between any of His messengers.
Paul says that eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, the things which God hath prepared for them that love Him.
The first letter of John says: it doth not yet appear what we shall be, but we shall see him as he is. Is knowledge through a mediator a condition of this life, or of every world?
Jesus told his disciples: it is expedient for you that I go away.
Plotinus likens what proceeds from the Supreme to the brilliant light encircling the sun.
Micah sums up what the Lord requires: to do justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God.
Seneca wrote that we need not beg a temple keeper for access: God is near you, he is with you, he is within you. If the divine is within, what are prophets for?

job-daysman-betwixt-us.text: For he is not a man, as I am, that I should answer him, and we should come together in judgment. Neither is there any daysman betwixt us, that might lay his hand upon us both

hebrews-mediator-of-a-better-covenant.text: But now hath he obtained a more excellent ministry, by how much also he is the mediator of a better covenant, which was established upon better promises

john-epistle-advocate-with-the-father.text: My little children, these things write I unto you, that ye sin not. And if any man sin, we have an advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous

hebrews-come-boldly.text: For we have not an high priest which cannot be touched with the feeling of our infirmities; but was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin. Let us therefore come boldly unto the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace to help in time of need

john-ask-the-father-in-my-name.text: Verily, verily, I say unto you, Whatsoever ye shall ask the Father in my name, he will give it you. Hitherto have ye asked nothing in my name: ask, and ye shall receive, that your joy may be full

john-he-that-receiveth-me.text: He that receiveth whomsoever I send receiveth me; and he that receiveth me receiveth him that sent me

hebrews-new-and-living-way.text: Having therefore, brethren, boldness to enter into the holiest by the blood of Jesus, By a new and living way, which he hath consecrated for us, through the veil, that is to say, his flesh

corinthians-ambassadors-for-christ.text: To wit, that God was in Christ, reconciling the world unto himself, not imputing their trespasses unto them; and hath committed unto us the word of reconciliation. Now then we are ambassadors for Christ, as though God did beseech you by us: we pray you in Christ's stead, be ye reconciled to God

exodus-moses-put-a-vail.text: And till Moses had done speaking with them, he put a vail on his face. But when Moses went in before the Lord to speak with him

quran-bring-us-near.text: Surely pure religion is for Allah only. And those who choose protecting friends beside Him (say): We worship them only that they may bring us near unto Allah. Lo! Allah will judge between them concerning that wherein they differ. Lo! Allah guideth not him who is a liar, an ingrate.

quran-turn-thy-face.text: So turn thy face toward the Inviolable Place of Worship, and ye (O Muslims), wheresoever ye may be, turn your faces (when ye pray) toward it

dhammapada-no-one-can-purify-another.text: By oneself the evil is done, by oneself one suffers; by oneself evil is left undone, by oneself one is purified. Purity and impurity belong to oneself, no one can purify another
